title: The Go build cache grows ~40 GB a day because every cycle builds in a new worktree path
summary: On 2026-09-29 ~/Library/Caches/go-build held 60 GB 27 hours after `go clean -cache`, with 48 GB unused for 6 hours. cmd/go's build action ID includes the package directory when -trimpath is off, so each cycle worktree (.evolve/worktrees/cycle-<hash>-<N>) re-caches the whole module in every mode it builds (-race, -tags acs, -cover, integration). `evolve gc` now trims entries unused past gc.go_cache_ttl_hours, which bounds the cache but not the churn (every cycle still rebuilds from cold and writes ~GBs).
fix: Remove the path from the cache key for pipeline builds. Candidates: stable lane worktree paths reused across cycles (lane slots), or -trimpath for the pipeline's own go invocations (the gates, the build floor, the ACS suite), after checking which tests locate files via runtime.Caller (trimpath makes those paths module-relative). Measure the cache bytes written per cycle before and after.
acceptance: Two consecutive cycles building the same packages hit the cache for unchanged packages (red today: a new worktree path misses)
The cache growth per cycle is measured and reported before and after
